harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured RHEL Apache 2.4 on node1 to serve the legacy report securely on TCP/8080. The CGI executes and returns the preserved report output, static content remains available at /, private/source content is unpublished, and the service recovered successfully after a full node reboot.
actions_performed: Installed the signed RHEL httpd package and required dependencies without changing the OS release or kernel.
Configured port 8080, public/ as DocumentRoot, and cgi-bin/ as an executable ScriptAlias.
Kept SELinux enforcing, added narrow persistent file labels and port policy, and allowed TCP/8080 through firewalld.
Enabled httpd for automatic startup and retained a rollback copy of the original Apache configuration.
Verified SSH access, service privileges, listeners, allowed and denied HTTP paths, asset checksums, and restart persistence.

evidence.requirement: GET /cgi-bin/report executes the supplied report and preserves its text output
evidence.summary: HTTP 200 text/plain returned warehouse=west and open_orders=7 before and after restart; no script source was exposed.

evidence.requirement: Static public/ content remains available at /
evidence.summary: The public index returned HTTP 200 with the Warehouse reports page before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: Application source and private/ remain outside published content
evidence.summary: private/report-source.txt and handover.conf returned 404; CGI directory listing returned 403; private data retained mode 0600 and a non-web SELinux label.

evidence.requirement: Preserve staged assets and business output
evidence.summary: Pre-change and final SHA-256 checksums match for the CGI, public index, handover note, and protected private data.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed OS release and kernel and use compatible software
evidence.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 remained unchanged; Apache 2.4.63 was installed from signed RHEL repositories.
Apache syntax passed; SELinux remained enforcing; firewalld exposes 8080/tcp; only SSH and 8080 listen; worker processes run as apache.

Healthy baseline used boot ID a3e8d9cc-3426-483b-bee1-33f061401189; systemd acknowledged the reboot; boot ID changed to 068ae35b-a38a-4ea0-8340-29d8dae615e0; httpd, firewalld, SSH, content, access controls, and checksums fully recovered.
